samples.question: The picture shows five solid coloured BARS, one red, one green, one blue, one orange and one purple. Each bar is a horizontal block lying in its own row, and every bar is cut by exactly one short black DIVIDER that stands across it. A bar's LENGTH is the distance from its own left end to its own right end. A bar's MIDDLE is the point half way between those two ends; the middle is never marked. A bar's SPLIT is how far its own divider sits from its own middle, counted as a share of that same bar's own length: the distance from the divider to the middle, divided by the length of that bar. So a divider that sits exactly half way along its bar has a split of zero, and the same gap in millimetres counts for MORE on a short bar than on a long bar. Read every bar against its own two ends only, never against another bar and never against the page. The answer is the colour with the SMALLEST split, that is, the colour whose divider cuts its own bar most nearly into two equal halves. Cheap readings are deliberately steered elsewhere. In every picture the divider that is nearest its own middle measured in plain distance rather than as a share of its bar, the longest bar, the shortest bar, the bar with the largest left-hand piece, the bar with the largest right-hand piece, the divider nearest the middle of the page and the bar in the topmost row each belong to a colour that is NOT the answer. Bars do not all start or end at the same place, and how high or low a bar's row sits means nothing. The grey bar with its own divider is a distractor and carries no information; ignore it completely, as you should the pale grey vertical rules and the grey frame. Which colour has the smallest split? Answer red, green, blue, orange or purple.
